Found 2026-08-15 while resolving a contradiction between two live surfaces.

## The contradiction

`basicly loop preflight` printed `checkpts: ship pending - the live L3 grant delegates it`
while the supervisor routed the same lane to `ship checkpoint awaiting human approval` on
257 consecutive rounds. Both lines were true.

## Cause - ship approval has two implementations and only one asks

| path | consults |
| --- | --- |
| `supervise._land_green` -> `policy.approve_checkpoint_guarded` (`supervise.py:3968-3974`) -> `policy._grant_approval` (`policy.py:1687-1760`) | the grant, the session tree, the spend halt, and lights-out violations. Correct. |
| `supervise.advance_parked` -> `loop.run_until_blocked` (`supervise.py:3519`) -> `loop._on_verify` (`loop.py:423-427`) | `policy.checkpoint_approved` (`policy.py:1188-1191`) - **a bare marker read** |

`run_until_blocked` does forward `grant_root` (`loop.py:2583, 2599`), but inside `advance`
that argument reaches only the spend gates (`loop.py:785, 810`) and proposal delegation
(`loop.py:1196`). `_on_verify` ignores it.

## Consequence

A lane that reaches verify without passing through `_land_green` - a mini-loop lane that
finished its sub-tasks inside `advance_parked`, or any lane re-adopted on a later round - is
checked against the marker alone and blocks forever under a grant that covers it. Observed
on 2026-08-15 with a live L3 grant whose `GRANT_COVERAGE` includes `ship`
(`policy.py:1467-1472`).

Preflight is right about the policy and the landing path honours it. The parked path is the
defect.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

Found 2026-08-15 while verifying the `basicly-u2hl.56` fix by hand.

`_on_verify` now resolves the ship checkpoint through `policy.approve_checkpoint_guarded`
with `ctx.grant_root`. The supervisor passes `session.root_issue`, so the supervised path
reaches the grant. `basicly loop advance` accepts no `--root`, so `ctx.grant_root` is None
and the guarded call defaults to the issue itself - which carries no grant when the grant is
on the epic.

Observed - `basicly loop advance basicly-b2n2` returns
`[blocked] verify -> verify: ship checkpoint awaiting human approval` while
`basicly loop preflight basicly-u2hl` reports `ship pending - the live L3 grant delegates
it`, because the grant is on `basicly-u2hl` and nothing tells `advance` so.

This is not the same defect as `u2hl.56`, which was the parked path not asking at all. This
is the hand path having no way to say which session it belongs to. `loop run` already takes
`--root` for exactly this.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the two surfaces side by side - this alone establishes the defect:

       uv run basicly loop advance --help
       uv run basicly loop run --help

   Observed 2026-08-19: `loop run` carries
   `--root ROOT   Session root issue whose autonomy grant may cover the checkpoints
   (default: the issue itself)`, and `loop advance` carries no `--root` at all - its options
   are `--work-type`, `--children`, `--mode`, `--runner`, `--autonomy` and nothing else.
2. Put an L3 grant on an epic and take one of its children to the ship checkpoint.
3. Ask the hand path to advance the child:

       uv run basicly loop advance <child-id>

4. Ask the preflight, on the epic, whether the grant covers that same ship:

       uv run basicly loop preflight <epic-id>

5. Read the code path that explains the disagreement:

       rg -n 'approve_checkpoint_guarded' src/basicly/loop.py
       rg -n 'grant_root' src/basicly/cli.py

Observed - this record's measurement 2026-08-15, verifying the `basicly-u2hl.56` fix by hand:
step 3 returned

    [blocked] verify -> verify: ship checkpoint awaiting human approval

while step 4 reported `ship pending - the live L3 grant delegates it`. `_on_verify` resolves
the ship checkpoint through `policy.approve_checkpoint_guarded` with `ctx.grant_root`; the
supervisor passes `session.root_issue` and so reaches the grant, but `loop advance` accepts no
`--root`, so `ctx.grant_root` is None and the guarded call defaults to the issue itself -
which carries no grant, because the grant is on the epic.

Expected: `loop advance` takes `--root` with the same meaning and default `loop run` already
gives it, so the hand path can name the session it belongs to and reaches the same grant the
supervised path does. This is not `basicly-u2hl.56`, which was the parked path not asking at
all; this is the hand path having no way to say which session it is in.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a grant on an epic and a child at the ship checkpoint when `basicly loop advance
  <child> --root <epic>` runs then the checkpoint is approved under that grant and the
  advance proceeds, rather than blocking on human approval.
- Given `basicly loop advance <child>` with no `--root` then the behaviour is unchanged, so
  the default stays the issue itself and nothing silently widens.
- Given `basicly loop advance --help` then `--root` is described in the same terms
  `loop run --help` uses, because two spellings of one concept is what this record is about.
- Given a `--root` naming a record that carries no grant then the advance blocks and says the
  named root carries no grant, rather than reporting the child's own absence of one.
- Demonstrated by: `uv run basicly loop advance <child> --root <epic>` advancing past the ship
  checkpoint, against a control run without `--root` on the same record that still blocks.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Context

The plan gate refuses a `demonstration` field that is absent, multi-line, or names
nothing backticked. `plan_gate.demonstration_fault` checks the field's **form** and
never runs the command, so a backticked span that selects **zero** tests passes.

Measured 2026-08-15: five beads were closed or worked in one session naming a
demonstration of the form `uv run pytest <file> -k <expr>` where the expression
selects zero tests, against positive controls collecting 210, 142, 87 and 23 in the
very files they name. Every real regression existed under another name and passed.
So the field was refused for being absent or unquoted, and accepted for being wrong.

Confirmed against the tree 2026-08-16: `plan_gate.py` contains no `subprocess` and no
`run(`, against a positive control of 5 occurrences in `verify.py`.

## Why a third form rule is not the answer

A form rule cannot tell a command that selects nothing from one that selects
everything. Running the criterion's own command and reading the collected count is
free, deterministic, and impossible to satisfy by rewording.

- Given a planned child whose demonstration names a pytest selector matching no test
  when the plan gate runs then the child is refused at the same rung as an absent
  field - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_plan_gate.py -k zero_selection -q`

payload.text:
[measured 2026-08-20, and the five unwired kinds are not one population but three]

The record says five kinds have no handoff.record caller and no entry_verdict reader. Confirmed, with a correction that changes what the build is for one of them. Positive control repo_root at 67 files, negative control at 0.

WIRED, three, each with a producer and a reader:
- implementation-plan: produced decompose.py:2031, read loop.py:361
- change-summary: produced loop.py:1579, read loop.py:2064
- release-record: produced curate.py:58, gated loop.py:670 on handoff.adopted

UNWIRED, and they split three ways by WHY, which is the thing the record asks to decide per kind:

1. PRODUCED BY THE MARKER PATH, SCHEMA UNEXERCISED. classification. It has a producer today, classify.py:74 calling _record_classification, persisting `[harness-classification]` as declared at integrity.py:52. So the data exists and the typed contract does not see it. This is a MIGRATION onto the typed-event path pp7q4i built, not a build from scratch, and it is the cheapest of the five by a wide margin.

2. SCHEDULED, PRODUCER ALREADY A RECORD. solution-design. It is the one kind with no schema at all. basicly-u2hl.19, emit a solution design at intake with six checked sections, is its producer and is in the ready set. So declaring it unwired today is correct and temporary, and the inventory should not treat it the same as a kind nobody has planned.

3. NO PRODUCER OF ANY KIND. change-shape, verification-evidence, validation-transcript. Each has a schema and zero references outside handoff.py and tests. Note validation-transcript is the odd one: loop._dispatch_validation already runs a validator whose output is a transcript in substance, so the artifact is unwired while the work it describes runs every validate. That is the strongest candidate of the three, and the weakest argument for deleting a schema.

A PROBE FAILURE WORTH RECORDING, because it is this repo's recurring trap. My first probe grepped the literal string `classification` and returned six files, which reads as a wired kind. Five of the six are the ENGLISH WORD or the marker constant, not the artifact kind. The discriminator is that a wired kind appears as a handoff.<CONST> symbol at its producer, per the control taken on curate.py:52 and :58; only three such constants exist in handoff.py. So the probe for wiredness is the constant, never the kind's name. A reader who greps the name will over count by one and conclude classification is wired.

THE DESIGN POINT THE BUILD MUST SETTLE FIRST, and it is the same trap this repo has paid for before. How does the inventory KNOW a kind is unwired. Deriving it from absence, no constant or no caller found, makes the check ambiguous between unwired and probed wrongly, which is exactly how my own six-file miss happened. Bind it on what the producer declares instead: let the kind list carry its producer symbol per kind, and let the inventory verify that symbol exists and is called. Then a kind with no declared producer is unwired BY DECLARATION and the gate cannot fail open. That also makes the three-way split above expressible, because a declared-but-scheduled kind and a declared-nothing kind stop looking identical.

WHAT THIS DID NOT ESTABLISH. Whether any of the four schema'd unwired kinds is read by a test in a way that would break if the schema changed, so a schema that refuses nothing in production may still be pinned by a fixture. Check `rg -l '<kind>' tests/` before proposing a deletion; a regenerated artifact in this repo usually has a captured fixture behind it.

## The defect

`basicly-vbl35a` made the cap stop cutting any key the fold reads, which acceptance criterion 1 required. The consequence it names rather than buries: `field`.`value` and every `created` payload key are now stored **whole** where `value` was previously cut at 4096 bytes, and **nothing in the tree bounds them**.

That is not a regression against the old behaviour for `created` — a description under `description` was always uncapped, and 31 are stored above 4096 with the largest at 7043. It **is** a new hole for `field`.`value`, which the cap did bound, wrongly, and now bounds not at all.

The reason the cap exists is section 32.10 first paragraph: git compression, the ship-time rollup and a change-sized write all assume bounded events, and none of them bounds a single pasted payload. An agent that pastes a multi-megabyte log into a description now puts it in every clone, compressed and unremovable, because true removal is the history rewrite section 32.8 forbids.

## Why the cap cannot be the answer

Cutting a folded field makes a derived value depend on the cap, which breaks the determinism section 32.2 asserts. So the bound has to move to the **producer**, which is D-36 derivability argument applied to a field rather than to an artifact: a body is bounded by dropping what the ledger can already derive, not by a byte count.

`basicly-gvlpxm` does exactly this for `change-summary`. It does not cover a folded field, so this record is the sibling case and not a duplicate.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Write a field event whose value is a 5 MB string through the engine seam.
2. Read the stored event. Observe the whole 5 MB, no truncation flag, and no refusal.
3. Confirm no gate refuses it: run the verify suite and observe every check pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a folded field whose value exceeds a declared producer bound then the write is refused at the seam with the field named, rather than stored.
Given a folded field within the bound then the write is unchanged and the fold derives the same state.
Given a refusal then it says which field and what the bound is, so the caller can drop what is derivable instead of guessing.
Given an existing oversized value already in the log then the fold derives the same state as before and nothing rewrites it.
Demonstrated by: uv run pytest tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py -q plus a seam-level test that a 5 MB field value is refused, against a positive control that a small one is accepted

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `tests/`

Two sites `basicly-vbl35a` left alone, both named in its own report rather than found later.

After vbl35a they are safe because they are **present in** `FOLD_READ_KEYS`. The assertions still pass, so no gate sees it, and an unverified test rationale pins the wrong invariant for the next reader.

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/migrate.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_provenance.py`

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## The defect

A `git push` that runs while a landing is in flight rolls back, and the reported cause names a stash rather than contention.

`pre-commit` 4.6.0 stashes unstaged changes before it runs a hook stage and restores them after. Our `pre-push` stage runs `.basicly/core/hooks/pre-push.py`. A landing that writes the ledger inside that window changes the tree under the stash, so the restore conflicts and the push aborts with `Stashed changes conflicted with hook auto-fixes`.

The commits themselves are intact. The operator loses the push and, worse, reads a stash message as a local mistake rather than as two engine operations racing.

This is the third surface of one contention class. `basicly-kjc5.63` is the same race on the base checkout commit during dispatch. `basicly-kjc5.62` is adjacent. On each surface the failure text names a git mechanism, never contention, so an operator diagnoses it wrongly every time.

## Why it has no record until now

It was carried as prose in `HANDOVER.md` and as a comment on another record, never as a record of its own. Measured 2026-08-20 over the 980 record ledger: a search of every record's fields for `Stashed changes conflicted` and for `pre.push.*stash` returns **zero**, against a mid frequency control of `rework` at **95** and a negative control at **0**. Seven sibling traps in the same handover each have a record; this one is the only one that does not.

That is the finding `basicly-askx4j` needs: the handover is almost entirely derivable, and this record is the positive instance of the one class it carried that the ledger did not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a landing that writes the ledger, for example `basicly loop run <id>` reaching its tracker commit, or any `basicly tracker write`.
2. While that write is in flight, run `git push` in the same checkout.
3. Observe `pre-commit` stash the unstaged tree for the `pre-push` stage.
4. Observe the landing write the ledger inside that window.
5. Observe the restore conflict and the push roll back with `Stashed changes conflicted with hook auto-fixes`.
6. Observe `git log` shows the commits are unharmed, so the message describes the stash and not the actual fault.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a ledger write in flight when a push reaches the pre-push stage then the push refuses with a message naming the contention and the operation that holds the tree, rather than reporting a stash conflict - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_hooks_pre_push.py -k contention -q`
- Given no ledger write in flight when a push reaches the pre-push stage then the push runs unchanged - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_hooks_pre_push.py -k quiet -q`

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/pre-push.py`
- `tests/test_hooks_pre_push.py`

## Working Set

- `.basicly/core/hooks/pre-push.py`
- `tests/test_hooks_pre_push.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_hooks_pre_push.py -q`

payload.text:
Closed by 0a0d669e. Full verify PASS, 31 checks, 4499 tests.

pre-push.py now asks whether a ledger write is in flight before it runs the checks, and refuses BEFORE pre-commit's stash exists - so there is nothing to conflict. The message says the three things the stash message withheld: which pid holds the tree, that the git text about to appear describes the stash and not the fault, and that the commits are unaffected.

Reuse over respelling: the lock's name and the liveness rule come from the kit's own events.py, loaded core-relative so hook and kit relocate together. Only .basicly/ledger is spelled at hook level, which tracker-path-scan.py:47 already does.

Fails quiet in every ambiguous case, deliberately: no kit, no lock, an unreadable lock, a dead pid, and the platform that cannot judge. Windows has no stdlib liveness probe because os.kill(pid, 0) there calls TerminateProcess and would kill the process it was asking about, so default_pid_liveness answers None. Refusing on the hook's own uncertainty would read as contention and would block every push on that platform for as long as a stale lock sat on disk. All three liveness answers are injected as test data, never raced.

Two mutations, each failing its own tests: dropping the liveness check, and never firing the guard. 11 tests; both acceptance selectors work.

TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN CHANGE WERE CAUGHT ONLY BY RUNNING THE REAL HOOK, not by its unit tests: a parenthesised except clause where nothing binds, which the house form forbids under PEP 758, and a dynamically loaded module typed as object, which broke pyright on every attribute it reached. The tests passed with both present. That is the validate-as-consumer rule earning itself on a 100-line hook.

Two probe errors of mine, both mine and not the code's. The first wrote a pid that had died between shell calls. The second used uv run --directory, which changes the working directory, so project_root found the basicly repo instead of the probe and the hook correctly reported no contention. The third attempt used a live child process and a cwd genuinely inside the probe, and the hook refused with exit 1 naming the pid.

Not done: the contention class itself. This makes one surface honest. basicly-kjc5.63 is the same race on the base checkout, and nothing yet holds a lock that both operations respect - the hook declines to push rather than the two serialising.

payload.description:
## Context

Step 3 of the cutover in `docs/design/work-tracker.md` §5. Steps 1 and 2 landed 2026-08-07
(`b97a653`, `17be554`).

**This is a config flip, not a code change.** `br._mirror_write` is already called on every
accepted write and is a no-op only in `MODE_EXTERNAL`, so setting `[tracker] mode = "dual"`
in `basicly.toml` activates it.

## Why it is now urgent rather than merely next

The first real shadow differential (2026-08-07) reported `clean: no, conclusive: yes` with
three records **unknown to the ledger** - `basicly-f6th`, `basicly-s5li`, `basicly-wpc8`,
all filed that same day, after the import. Nothing keeps the ledger current in `external`
mode, so that count grows with every bead filed. Three in a single working day.

**Do not fix this by re-importing.** `import_snapshot` is upsert, so a re-import would
quietly add the missing records and make the differential look cleaner - but the owned side
would then be tracking the external side, and the agreement would prove nothing. That is the
§5.1 self-agreement trap reached by a second route. Dual write is the answer, and until it is
on, every day in shadow mode adds noise the differential cannot distinguish from a real
defect.

## Pre-flight, measured 2026-08-07 - the flip will not hard-fail

A mirror failure **raises** rather than logging (`_mirror_write` docstring: "Every failure
below is raised, never logged, and that is the acceptance criterion"), and an unknown write
surface or unknown `br update` flag raises `TrackerDivergenceError`. So the flip is safe only
if every write surface the engine spawns has a translator. Checked:

- `_MIRRORED_WRITES` covers `close`, `comments add`, `create`, `dep add`, `gate report`,
  `update`.
- Those are exactly the six surfaces `classify_access` calls `write` among everything the
  engine spawns. Every other spawned surface - `comments list`, `dep cycles`, `gate list`,
  `show`, `blocked`, `lint`, `where` - classifies `read` and returns no drafts.
- `sync` and `init` are in `_UNMIRRORED_WRITES` deliberately; they are br-only surfaces with
  no owned equivalent. Note `init` classifies as `unclassified`, so it is excluded by the
  list rather than by classification - correct today, but it depends on the list.
- `br update` is spawned with only `-t` and `--external-ref`, exactly the two flags the
  mapping declares plus status.

## Sequencing constraint

Do not flip while a lane is mid-flight. Because a mirror failure raises, an uncovered write
would fail a running lane tracker write rather than degrading. Flip from a clean base with no
live worktrees, then exercise it before dispatching anything.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given basicly.toml at tracker mode dual when a bead is created and a comment and a gate result and a dependency are written then each appears in the owned ledger as well as in br and a subsequent shadow differential reports no record unknown to the ledger for anything written after the flip

## Scope

- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_br_seam.py`
payload.title: Flip the tracker to dual write and stop the ledger drifting

payload.text:
Sequencing note: this is step 3 in the design and it is blocked on basicly-s5li, which is step 5. The inversion is deliberate, for two reasons.

Technical: s5li changes how the harness markers are written - from br comments to native ledger events. Dual write mirrors the write path, so flipping first would spend a window mirroring a shape we are about to replace, and every mirrored comment written in that window becomes history in the ledger under the old shape.

Operational: the flip is unsafe while a lane is in flight, because a mirror failure raises rather than degrading, so an uncovered write surface would fail a running lane rather than logging. s5li was dispatched before this bead was filed.

The design numbering is a narrative order, not a dependency. Step 2 (shadow) genuinely had to precede this one and did.

[harness-info] the cutover sequence is now buildable, 2026-08-14

`basicly-vkh0.23` landed `basicly tracker import` and `basicly-c357` landed the flip boundary.
Together they resolve a tension that reads like a contradiction in the two beads and is not one.

## The apparent contradiction

This bead says do not re-import, because the owned side would then be tracking the external side
and the agreement would prove nothing. `c357` says the 200 historical records stay unimported and
named. Read together those imply the ledger reaches `owned` **missing 200 real beads**, which
would be data loss rather than a design.

## The sequence that resolves it

The order is what matters, not whether an import ever runs:

```text
1  basicly tracker import                  bring the ledger current, while still `external`
2  basicly tracker shadow --declare-history declare whatever delta remains (ideally none)
3  flip to `dual`                           the dual write begins
4  basicly tracker shadow                   now judged over a non-empty post-flip scope
```

Importing at step 1 is **not** the re-import this bead refuses. What it refuses is closing the gap
*after* the dual write has started, when the agreement being measured is the dual write. Before
the flip there is no dual write to prove anything about, so bringing the ledger current is
housekeeping. The controls make that distinction mechanical rather than a matter of discipline:

- `basicly tracker import` **refuses a ledger that already holds a post-flip record**, so step 1
  cannot be re-run after step 3 to tidy a failure away.
- `shadow --declare-history` **refuses a second declaration**, so the baseline cannot be widened
  after step 3 either.

## What this bead still owes

payload.description:
## Context

`board_facts.document` takes `in_flight` defaulting to False and emits the `lanes` section only when it is True. Exactly one caller passes True: `board_facts.emit_tick` at src/basicly/board_facts.py:572, the supervisor 15-second beat. Both one-shot producers call the bare form - `board_cli.py:97` for `basicly board --out` and `board_cli.py:135` for the server `build` callback - so neither emits it.

Measured 2026-09-01 on this checkout:

```text
board_facts.document(Path(".")) -> lanes present: False
```

The consequence is that on any repo with no supervisor running, `running now` reads `not emitted by this producer` and the loop note reads `current position: lanes not emitted by this producer`. Two markers, and the section can never say anything else. A live supervisor replaces the whole document with its own tick file, which does emit lanes, so the section works only in the state where an operator least needs to be told what is running.

The omission is deliberate and the reason is recorded at the parameter: Mode A and Mode B fold whatever lock they find without knowing its selector, so a label pass drawn from there would name the root children instead of the lanes in flight. That constraint is real. It argues for a different reading, not for silence - the same document already distinguishes `no lane is dispatched` from an absent producer, and a checkout with no supervisor has a true answer to give.

This is the third instance of the shape basicly-bd4epr closed for the opposite direction. That record closed on a live-supervisor page; the unsupervised page was never the control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the board is folded with no supervisor lock held, THE `running now` SECTION SHALL read that no pass is running rather than that no producer emitted it.
- WHEN a supervisor lock is held, THE SECTION SHALL keep reading the tick producer lanes unchanged.
- WHERE the producer cannot know the pass selector, IT SHALL NOT name any bead as in flight.
- WHEN `basicly board --out` runs on this checkout with no supervisor, ITS output SHALL carry no `not emitted by this producer` marker for lanes.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_cli.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L2
- demonstration: `basicly board --out` with no supervisor running draws a running-now section that names the idle state

payload.text:
[harness-info] Proof-run plan, drafted 2026-07-26 with the owner. Two corrections to the initial framing are recorded first because they change the risk.

Correction 1 - jr0l is not a low-risk root. It has 20 non-closed children, 19 ready, and the scheduler ranks by priority and score rather than by risk. The lanes it would actually dispatch are kjc5.29 (rank 8, refuse to dispatch an unresolved model - on the critical path to 7bur), kjc5.32 (rank 10, coupling attribution - should precede Phase 5), then kjc5.49, kjc5.50, kjc5.51. Those are real Phase 1/5/7 work, not the catalog capacity fillers the root was chosen for. There is no single root that isolates only the low-risk beads.

Correction 2 - the spend ceiling exists only on a grant. policy.spend_status returns halted=False outright when no grant is active, so at true L0 there is no token cap and the halt predicate is inert. There is no [policy.spend] section anywhere. GRANT_COVERAGE resolves it: L1 delegates only the decompose checkpoint, which a leaf bead never reaches, so an L1 grant carrying a token_budget gives a hard ceiling while leaving classify and ship human on every lane.

Decided with the owner: root basicly-jr0l; autonomy raised one notch to L1 in basicly.toml solely to make the grant issuable, with an L1 grant of 1000000 tokens; every classify and ship checkpoint answered by a human with a minted confirm code; the ceiling reverted to L0 after the run.

Known wart: loop supervise takes only the issue argument, so both the runner and the autonomy ceiling have to be changed repo-wide in basicly.toml for the duration and reverted after. That is exactly what basicly-jr0l.8 exists to fix and it is still open, so doing jr0l.8 first would remove two config round-trips from this procedure.

Also required: [runner] default is currently manual, with a comment that auto-dispatch would double-run the interactively driven loop. It must become a real agent (claude and copilot are both on PATH) for the run to dispatch at all, and revert afterwards.

Pre-flight, before any tokens: basicly runner dry-run to verify the dispatch command; basicly decompose --dry-run on each candidate lane for the sizing verdict, because cost is bounded by sizing the work and never by killing an agent; confirm base is clean and no supervisor lock is held; and fix the intervention tally definition in advance - a checkpoint approval is by design and does not count, an intervention caused by a harness defect does.

Measurement to record: total tokens against the 3.36M baseline, wall clock, lanes landed, and every intervention with its cause. The acceptance criterion is zero interventions attributable to a harness defect.

[harness-info] Proof run executed 2026-07-26. The acceptance criterion is NOT met, and the run cost 34.16 dollars for 46026602 tokens across three lanes.

What worked. Everything built earlier in the session behaved: the session overrides applied with no committed config touched (jr0l.8, jr0l.15), all three lanes were adopted and dispatched concurrently, progress was visible live through a pipe (8veb), the halt surfaced as a queue item rather than a silent stall, and jr0l.17 correctly reported spend under this grant rather than lifetime. Two lanes landed through the merge queue; the third was cancelled pre-landing by D5 when a sibling landing moved its base, then landed by hand from its committed branch at no extra cost. All three shipped. The suite went 1360 to 1415 tests, all green. kjc5.51 honoured the [harness-wait] comment-marker constraint amended into its AC, so the section 3.4 discipline held under an unsupervised agent.

Interventions attributable to a harness defect: two.

1. The grant budget metered lifetime session spend, so a 5M ceiling halted before dispatching once against 30705839 tokens of history. Fixed mid-run as basicly-jr0l.17.
2. The forecast was wrong by two to three orders of magnitude, so the ceiling admitted a pass that spent nine times it. Now basicly-jr0l.21 (forecast spend and wall clock per model) and basicly-jr0l.22 (admit a pass on forecast spend), with basicly-kjc5.29 promoted to a prerequisite of both.

Ship checkpoints and the D5 re-dispatch do not count - those are by design.

Owner correction that settled the diagnosis: the admission gate is right and must stay. Cost is bounded by sizing the work, never by killing a working agent. The defect is the forecast, and the decomposition has to cut work so each lane is optimally sized - which means learning actual tokens and wall clock per unit of work, per model, because different models need different amounts and models change constantly.

This bead is now blocked on jr0l.22, so a re-run is gated on the spend forecast existing. That is deliberate: repeating this run today would be financially unsafe, not merely inconclusive.

[harness-info] Proof-run budget set 2026-07-29 by the owner delegating the call. Grant L1 with a 10000000 token ceiling. Derivation: the successful kjc5.22 dogfood spent 3360000 tokens across three lanes, so 10M leaves about 3x headroom for a correctly sized pass while the 46026602 tokens of the failed attempt is refused at admission once basicly-jr0l.22 makes the gate predictive. At the blended rate the failed run itself demonstrated - 34.16 dollars over 46026602 tokens, about 0.74 dollars per million - that ceiling caps the proof at roughly 7 to 8 dollars against the 34.16 it cost last time. Recorded rather than asserted so the number can be checked.

[harness-info] Third attempt, 2026-08-01, deliberately run as ONE lane rather than the
three-to-five lane shape, because the pre-flight found the cost gates inert (basicly-vz78). The
acceptance criterion is still NOT met - not because a lane failed, but because the run could not
be scaled safely and the intervention count is not yet measurable at the intended shape.

What the single lane proved, and it is real. `basicly-jr0l.40` was dispatched headless via
`claude -p`, worked unattended for 519.6s, and committed
`4bbb362 fix(policy): cover a gating track under an autonomy grant and report its size
(basicly-jr0l.40)` on its own branch: policy.py and cli.py changed, 129 lines of new tests across
tests/test_policy.py and tests/test_cli_policy.py, CHANGELOG.md and docs/design/factory-design.md
updated, worktree left clean. It satisfied the commit-msg gate (Conventional Commits plus the
trailing beads id) with no help. No human edited code.

Two procedural corrections to the plan recorded on this bead.

1. The procedure as written dispatches nothing. `basicly loop supervise <root>` alone prints
   "dispatch: (no ready build-phase lanes)" and stops, because `ready_lanes` requires a lane at
   phase `build` and every open bead derives `intake`. Nothing in the supervise loop advances a
   lane out of intake or provisions its worktree. The missing step is a seeding advance,
   `basicly loop run <root> --root <root>`, whose decompose->build transition calls
   `_ensure_child_worktrees`; a bound worktree is what derives `build` (loop_state.derive_phase,
   the ("build", worktree is not None) rung). Verified at zero cost before spending. The L1 grant
   earns its keep exactly there - it auto-approved the root's decompose checkpoint with no
   keystroke.
2. The cost estimate on this bead is wrong in both directions. Measured: 4079243 tokens and
   3.657368 USD for ONE lane, a blended 0.897 USD per million rather than 0.74. Five such lanes
   is about 20.4M tokens and 18.29 USD, not the 7 to 8 USD recorded here, and the 10M ceiling
   would not have bounded it because admission is read once per pass before dispatch. See
   basicly-vz78, which this bead now blocks on.

Interventions attributable to a harness defect: zero in the lane itself. One landing was refused
because the base checkout was dirty (the operator's own config edit plus tracker writes), which
is the basicly-4psl guard behaving correctly, not a defect.

Not yet demonstrated, and what a re-run still owes: concurrent multi-lane dispatch, the serial
merge queue under contention, and an intervention tally at the intended shape. All three are
gated on basicly-vz78, because at the measured per-lane cost an unbounded multi-lane pass is a
financial risk rather than an inconclusive one.

PROOF RUN 2026-08-07 - the dogfood shape re-run as a supervised multi-lane pass. Result: the acceptance criterion is NOT met. One intervention is attributable to a harness defect, so this bead stays open.

SHAPE. 'basicly loop supervise basicly-m4zv' with three concurrent lanes (m4zv.2, .4, .6) on real Phase-2 work, preceded by a single-lane 'loop run' of basicly-u6jq.2. Grants: L3/50M on basicly-u6jq, L3/60M on basicly-m4zv. Total metered spend 53,215,539 tokens across 6 run records, all outcome=executed, no lane killed and no runner_timeout.

INTERVENTION COUNT: 4 human decisions, of which 3 are by design and 1 is a harness defect.

1. BY DESIGN - the [catalog] rank1_floor value on m4zv.2. Plan section 7.5 reserves it as an owner decision 'deliberately not guessable'. The lane measured the baseline (80/87 = 92.0%), built everything else green, and raised needs-input rather than inventing a number. The decider was invoked and also declined, correctly: 'Any number I gave would be preference, not derivation.' This is block-don't-guess working, not a defect.

2 and 3. BY DESIGN - the ship checkpoints on m4zv.4 and m4zv.6. Both merged and green, both declined by the L3 grant citing 'lights-out preconditions across session basicly-m4zv: 1 needs-input event(s) recorded on basicly-m4zv.2'. policy.py:2081 states the rule deliberately: 'an unanswered ask on open work refuses a delegated ship, unchanged.' Once item 1 was answered, both delegated with no further human input - probed directly rather than read off the decision list, which still showed frozen text from the earlier pass. basicly-jr0l.65's answered-discount works; it did NOT regress.

4. HARNESS DEFECT - basicly-69az blocked m4zv.2's landing entirely. Fourth reproduction, and the first with no route: the lane adds a config key and declares it, the landing validates with the pre-merge engine and refuses the unknown key, and the documented schema-first workaround does not apply because four repo-state tests require the declaration. Cost one lane re-dispatch and a hand landing (rebase, merge --no-ff, verify from base with the merged engine, then ship). Full analysis recorded on basicly-69az.

WHAT WORKED UNATTENDED. Three lanes provisioned and dispatched concurrently; classify delegated on all three; zero cross-lane file collisions; the serial merge queue landed two lanes without conflict; docs-claims stayed current across both rebases so basicly-jr0l.68 did not fire; no human edited any code. Two of three lanes went build to merge to ship with no human input at all once the design question was answered.

BLOCKER. This bead now depends on basicly-69az. Re-run the proof after 69az is fixed - the run is otherwise reusable as-is.

basicly-jk3l closed 2026-08-13 as discharged; its survivability and observability preconditions were its four blockers, all closed: yvx9 (a killed lane commits its work), rupz (the dispatch event stream is read not discarded), 1lpo (a release epic can fan out), lpsf (the wall clock retired as a lane bound). Its edge to this bead was backwards - jk3l existed to enable this run, not to wait on it - and was removed rather than satisfied. Carry its criteria here: a pass is survivable and observable before this proof is attempted.

## Context

Found 2026-08-06 while sprinting at the `v0.8.0` cut. The owner's framing is the requirement:
basicly is a **dark factory** - once a human has clarified and grounded the requirements, alone
or with an agent, the workflow should be able to deliver on its own. It should not wait for a
human to *request* classification or decomposition.

Today it does. Two phases block on an input the loop cannot produce:

```python
# loop.py:238
return _blocked(ctx, "classify needs an agent-proposed work type", needs_input="work_type")
# loop.py:269
return _blocked(ctx, "decompose needs an agent-proposed child plan", needs_input="children")
```

Both arrive from *outside* the loop - `loop advance --work-type`, `loop advance --children`,
`basicly decompose --plan`. The docstring at `loop.py:251` already calls it "an agent-proposed
child plan", so the design intends an agent to propose it. No dispatch produces one.

## The gate held; that is the point

This is not a skipped phase. Measured 2026-08-06: `basicly loop status basicly-vkh0` reports
`phase: decompose`, and `basicly-vkh0` is **P0 and the single biggest `1.0.0` blocker**. It has
been parked there for sessions while 80+ ready leaves stayed dispatchable, because the one input
that would release it is one only a human hands in. The plan records the consequence in its own
words at `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` section 6: "Decompose first - the build has no beads
yet."

So the defect is not that the phase is unenforced. It is that the phase has **no delegated
producer**, and nothing anywhere surfaces "your P0 is blocked on an input only you can supply".
A supervised pass fans out over dependents, so an undecomposed epic is simultaneously
unworkable and invisible to the fan-out.

## The grant's wording makes it worse

`basicly policy grant` reports `delegable: classify, decompose, ship`. That reads as "the loop
will classify and decompose for you". It does not. Two distinct gates sit at each phase and only
the second is delegated:

| Gate | Site | Delegated under L3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Produce the work type / the child plan | `loop.py:238`, `loop.py:269` | no - no producer exists |
| Approve the classify / decompose checkpoint | `loop.py:285` | yes |

An operator reading the grant line reasonably concludes the factory is autonomous at these
phases. Whatever the fix, that wording has to stop implying a capability the engine lacks.

## Shape to consider

A delegated proposer dispatch, gated by the grant the same way every other delegation is: ask
the agent for the work type at intake and for a child plan at classify, validate what comes back
against the schema `decompose` already enforces (it refuses a child under `working_set_min` and
reports parallel groups, so a bad plan fails loudly rather than landing), and fall back to the
existing `needs_input` block when no grant permits the delegation or the proposal fails
validation. The autonomy ladder already draws the line this needs: L0/L1 keeps today's
human-supplied behaviour, L2+ may propose.

Worth noting the schema half is already built and load-bearing - a hand-authored plan for
`basicly-vkh0` was refused on 2026-08-06 for a child estimated at 4794 working-set tokens against
a floor of 8000. So a proposer's output has a real gate to pass, which is what makes delegating
it defensible rather than a licence to invent children.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
basicly loop status basicly-vkh0     # phase: decompose, and it stays there
basicly loop run basicly-vkh0        # blocks: decompose needs an agent-proposed child plan
```

Observed - the loop stops and waits for a human to author and hand in a plan. Expected under a
grant that permits it - the loop proposes one, validates it, and continues.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

## Context

`loop preflight` forecasts a pass at `per_lane x min(concurrency, open_children)`.
Provisioning does not use `concurrency`; `loop._ensure_child_worktrees` computes
`room = wt_config.concurrency - len(existing)` and seeds at most that many. So the
forecast over-states by exactly the number of worktrees already live.

Measured 2026-08-16 on `basicly-e2mz`, with 2 live worktrees and `concurrency = 5`:

```
worktrees: 2 live
forecast:  ~110949235 tokens if all 5 lanes start (per-lane x min(cap 5, 39 open))
```

The pass can seed 3 lanes, not 5. The honest forecast is ~66,569,541.

## Why the size of the error matters rather than the error

The figure exists to size a grant. An operator reading 110,949,235 against a
100,000,000 grant concludes the pass cannot run and either mints a larger grant than
the work needs or does not run it. Both were nearly done here. `admit_pass_spend`
totals the pass and refuses the whole thing on one violation, so the number a human
compares against the grant is the number that decides whether anything is dispatched
at all.

The preflight's own docstring states the intent — "the interesting number is what a
*full* fan-out would need, because that is what a budget has to be minted for" — and a
full fan-out is bounded by room, not by the cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given live worktrees exist when the preflight forecasts a pass then the lane count
  is the room provisioning would use rather than the raw cap - check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`
- Given no live worktrees then the forecast is unchanged - check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the cap and count the worktrees already live:

       rg -n '^concurrency' basicly.toml
       git worktree list

   `cli._print_preflight_spend` prices `priced = min(cap, open_count)` on the line it
   prints as `forecast:`; provisioning computes `room = wt_config.concurrency -
   len(existing)` in `loop._ensure_child_worktrees`. Nothing subtracts `len(existing)`
   on the forecast path.
3. Run the forecast on a root with open children but no dispatchable lane - that is the
   only branch which prints it, because `_print_preflight_spend` returns early as soon as
   `supervise.ready_lanes` is non-empty:

       uv run basicly loop preflight <root>

4. Read the `forecast:` line, then multiply its `per-lane:` figure by the room from step 1
   by hand and compare.

Observed - this record's own measurement, 2026-08-16 on `basicly-e2mz` with 2 live
worktrees and `concurrency = 5`:

    worktrees: 2 live
    forecast:  ~110949235 tokens if all 5 lanes start (per-lane x min(cap 5, 39 open))

The pass could seed 3 lanes; the honest figure was ~66,569,541. Re-checked in this checkout
2026-08-19: `git worktree list` shows **4** lane worktrees against `concurrency = 5`, so
room is 1 while the forecast would still price 5 - the inputs have made the error larger,
not smaller.

Expected: the forecast prices the room provisioning would use, and its parenthetical names
room rather than the raw cap.

- Given live worktrees exist when the preflight forecasts a pass then the lane count
  is the room provisioning would use rather than the raw cap - check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`
- Given no live worktrees then the forecast is unchanged - check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`

`uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`

payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-09-05: *"the diagram size and font does not fit the backlog 'next up' font size."*

Measured on the served document at 1920x1080. `max-height: 260px` against a `286`-unit viewBox scales the whole drawing by `260/286 = 0.909`:

| element | rendered |
| --- | --- |
| `NEXT UP` row title | **17px** |
| station name (`classify`) | **13.6px** |
| artifact and agent labels | **10px** |

So the region a reader looks at first carries type 20% smaller than the list beneath it, and its edge labels are the smallest text anywhere on the page. The hierarchy is inverted.

And the width is wasted. `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"` fits the drawing to the height and centres it, so it occupies **1091px inside a ~1900px region — 809px, 43%, is empty**.

## The cause is not the type sizes

Scaling the SVG scales the type with it, so raising a `font-size` inside the viewBox and leaving `max-height` alone changes nothing a reader can measure. The drawing has to be **wider and shorter** for its type to come out at the page's size — which is the same trade `basicly-6c97zx` already made twice, at `112px` when a pass runs and `display: none` under a 1000px wall.

## And it is spending that space on almost nothing

The live station counts are `1, 26, 1, 0, 0, 0` while the two terminals hold `263` and `936`. The census strip immediately below repeats all six numbers verbatim. So the page's largest region draws six near-zero figures twice.

That is the real finding: the diagram is oversized and under-typed because it has little to show. Any fix that only rescales it leaves a bigger drawing of the same six numbers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the diagram renders, ITS STATION LABELS SHALL be at least the size of a `NEXT UP` row, measured on the rendered page and not in viewBox units.
- WHEN the diagram renders at a claimed width, IT SHALL use that width, and the unused fraction SHALL be under 10 percent.
- WHERE the diagram and the census draw the same figures, ONE OF THEM SHALL go, and the record SHALL say which and why.
- WHEN the region is changed, `check_render_overflow.py` SHALL report nothing clipped and nothing overlapped at 1440x900, 1600x1200 and 1920x1080, in both the idle and the running-pass states.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_diagram.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_diagram.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: Screenshot the board and read a station label against a `NEXT UP` row, then run the overflow instrument at the three widths.

## Context

Parent: basicly-lc2bd3v. This is the control that stops the board drifting back into a report.

The owner has restated the cockpit requirement more than once, and each restatement is evidence the previous one did not hold. A requirement a person has to repeat is a requirement with no gate behind it.

The owner`s own test: *"if you as an agent look at the board, and only have access to the board, would you be able to see what is going on?"*

## What the gate is

One test that enumerates the nine questions and asserts each is answerable from the rendered page - not from the snapshot, and not from the model, because both have passed while the page drew nothing (basicly-3qstvw, basicly-yj8hpjr).

1. what work is available
2. what can start now
3. what is in progress, and who holds it
4. what is blocked, and by what
5. what one record actually says
6. how to start a record
7. how to stop a lane
8. how to descope a record
9. when the work will be done

## Acceptance Criteria

- THE TEST SHALL assert against the rendered page, using a fixture whose sections are all present.
- EACH question SHALL be one named assertion, so a failure names the question that stopped being answerable.
- WHERE a question is not yet answerable, THE TEST SHALL name the open record that will answer it and skip on that record alone, so the count of unanswered questions is visible and shrinks.

## Scope

- `tests/test_board_operator_questions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: delete a region from the template and watch the named question fail

Phase S's wired-or-deleted gate. Filed 2026-08-03; it was a row in the plan with no bead, which is the pattern the phase exists to remove.

Nothing merges without a reference from outside its own module and outside tests/. The evidence that this is needed is that every Phase S defect is one shape: an instrument built and never connected. permissions-check shipped wired to no gate; the import contract forbade modules that cannot exist and reported 1 kept 0 broken forever; .scripts/recall_eval.py was built, run once and wired to nothing.

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a dispatch dies before the model produces a token, I want the engine to stop re-dispatching that record, so I can stop a single launch defect from spending a pass and burying the real failure rate.

## Steps to Reproduce

Make a dispatch fail at launch, for example by naming an agent role the host does not have. Run a supervised pass over a record in that state. Observe the engine re-dispatch it without bound.

Observed in the recorded history [measured 2026-09-13 over 561 claude run records]: 110 runs died in under ten seconds, all in August, 97 of them on two days. `basicly-rn0o.6` holds 72 run records of which 60 are sub-ten-second failures on 2026-08-22. Stripping those two days moves the lifetime failure rate from 27.1 percent to 11.9 percent.

## Requirements

R1. One broken record cannot consume a pass.
R2. The failure rate the health view reports reflects work that was attempted, not a retry storm.
R3. An operator can tell a record stopped for repeated launch failure from one stopped for any other reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a record's dispatches fail consecutively up to the configured ceiling, then the engine stops dispatching it and records why. [check: `tests/test_supervise_admission.py`]
- When a dispatch of that record later succeeds, then the consecutive count resets. [check: `tests/test_supervise_admission.py`]
- When the ceiling stops a record, then the stop names the record, the count and the last failure. [check: `tests/test_supervise_admission.py`]
- When the ceiling is not configured, then a default applies rather than no bound at all. [check: `tests/test_config.py`]

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_supervise_admission.py -q`

## Design notes

Architecture section 28.2, where this becomes a seventh admission gate. A launch failure is distinguishable from a work failure by its duration and by the absence of a result event.
